task: measure the secretlint gate cost and add batch/per-file parity coverage
notes: profiled the last 1082ms gate step: npx 1032ms vs direct cached binary 619ms, npx --offline 922ms, npm exec 1061ms, so ~400ms is npm bootstrap and 619ms is real scanning of 655 files; narrowing to tracked files was slower (1524ms) and dropping npx would need a package.json dependency or stale-rule risk, so no change made. Instead added tests/test-skill-validation-cache.bats asserting the batched frontmatter cache prints byte-identical transcripts to the per-file python path on clean, warning, error and tab-in-path fixtures. The new test immediately caught a real drift: cache-hit issues were printed through the RED/NC escapes while the python path printed plain, so the same failure differed by code path; fixed to byte-identical output. 3 new tests, 29 in the touched files, full suite 355 ok, strict gate 0 skips
